title: Retro phase stalls with ZERO tokens — the pasted prompt sits unsubmitted in the claude-tmux pane (prompt-delivery regression recurrence), cascading into artifact-timeout + 3-block contract circuit + FAIL
summary: Cycles 1505 and 1510 (batches 20260817b/20260818a): the retrospective dispatch launched claude-tmux, the REPL prompt was detected, the prompt was pasted — and NOTHING was ever generated (retro-usage.json: input=0 output=0, cost 0, ~30min wall each). Both escalation reports' final_pane show PROMPT TEXT sitting visibly in the pane (1510: the persona's '## Final checks before exit' section; 1505: the '## Cycle Context' block) — pasted but never submitted. The observer pauses on artifact_timeout after 900s; the contract gate then blocks the missing artifact 3x, circuit-opens (gate demoted for the rest of the run), and the cycle FAILs having done the work-phases fine.
root_cause: Prompt submission failure on the claude-tmux driver for the RETRO dispatch specifically — the paste lands, the submitting Enter does not take effect (paste-buffer/bracketed-paste race, or prompt size: retro carries persona + full cycle artifacts, plausibly the largest prompt of the spine). Same family as the claude-tmux prompt-delivery regression fixed 2026-06-26 — either recurred or a size-dependent variant that fix did not cover. SECONDARY (same dispatch): "model='auto' is an unresolved tier token -> no --model sent" — the retro advisor overlay passes a tier token the resolver does not map, so the pane runs the CLI default model (routing wart; possibly the overlay-family-name-transport-ambiguity 0.87 class).
fix: (1) Reproduce with the REAL cycle-1510 prompt bytes (retrospective-prompt.txt preserved) against a live claude-tmux pane; instrument whether the Enter keypress lands (tmux send-keys sequencing vs paste-buffer completion). (2) Fix at the driver: after paste, verify the pane's input line is EMPTY (submitted) within a short window; if the prompt text is still visible at the input, re-send Enter (bounded retries, loud) — a deterministic submit-verify loop kills the class for every phase, not just retro. (3) The observer should classify 'zero tokens + prompt visible in final_pane' as delivery-failure (typed, retryable at dispatch level) instead of generic artifact_timeout — a fresh relaunch of the SAME dispatch would likely succeed and costs less than the 3-block circuit + FAIL cascade. (4) Separately resolve the 'auto' tier token at the retro overlay (map or reject loudly). Red-first: driver test with a large prompt fixture must observe submit-verify; observer classification test on the 1510 escalation-report shape.
files: go/internal/core/phase_advisor.go (the 'auto' tier token source for retro)
acceptance: Driver: after paste, an unsubmitted input line is detected and Enter re-sent (bounded, loud) — red-first with a large-prompt fixture.
Observer: zero-tokens + prompt-visible final_pane classifies as delivery-failure and triggers ONE dispatch-level relaunch before any artifact-timeout pause.
Retro dispatch never receives an unresolved tier token (map 'auto' or fail loudly at the overlay).
go vet + bridge suites + -race green; the 2 live escalation-report fixtures pinned.
connects_to: claude_tmux_prompt_delivery_regression (2026-06-26 fix — this is its recurrence/variant)
retro_always_on_failure standing rule (this class breaks the failure-learning loop wholesale)
contract-correction-stale-artifact-freshness 0.90 (the 3-block cascade this feeds is that item's no-rewrite shape: corrections re-validated an artifact no agent ever wrote)
notes: Filed from live console forensics: both occurrences have zero-token usage records and prompt-text final_panes preserved. Note the compounding: every FAIL cycle now ALSO burns ~30min + a contract circuit on the broken retro, and the failure-learning artifacts (lessons, dispositions) are never minted.
